findings.element: Row actions — the "Sync" / "Retry" / "View sync" link in the Actions column, and every item in the row ⋯ menu
findings.finding: The per-row primary action is an <a> with an onclick and no href, and all ⋯ menu items are plain <div class="dd-item"> — none of them has an href, tabindex or role, so none is in the tab order or operable by keyboard.
findings.user_impact: A keyboard or screen-reader user cannot sync, retry, roll back or archive an individual transaction at all — the entire per-row half of the primary task is unreachable, leaving only the checkbox-plus-bulk-bar path.
findings.suggested_fix: Make .row-action a real <button> and render each dd-item as a <button role="menuitem"> inside a role="menu", with arrow-key navigation and focus moved into the menu on open and back to the ⋯ trigger on close.

evidence.action: Tab through one table row (source traversal of the row template, index.html:2596-2613)
evidence.observed: Focus stops at the row checkbox, then the transaction-ID link (href="#"), then the ⋯ button — and then leaves the row. The Actions link `<a class="row-action" onclick="showPage('detail')">` is skipped because it has no href; activating the ⋯ button renders a menu of divs and focus stays on the trigger, since the file contains zero .focus() calls.

findings.element: Selection controls — 25 .row-chk row checkboxes, #chk-all, #chk-all-bulk, and the "Select all 31" scope link in the bulk bar
findings.finding: None of the 27 selection checkboxes has a label, aria-label or aria-labelledby, and the scope escalation to all 31 rows is an <a onclick> with no href, tabindex or role.
findings.user_impact: A screen-reader user hears "checkbox, unchecked" twenty-seven times with nothing to say which transaction each one selects, and a keyboard user can never widen selection past the 25 rows on page 1 before firing a bulk Archive or Sync.
findings.suggested_fix: Give each row checkbox an aria-label naming its transaction ("Select Nadia Rahman, $340.00, Failed"), label the two select-all boxes "Select all on this page", and make "Select all 31" a <button>.

evidence.action: Tab into the bulk bar after checking the header select-all (index.html:2279, 2293, 2313-2316, 2597)
evidence.observed: `` and `` carry no naming attribute of any kind, so the accessible name is empty; focus moves from #chk-all-bulk straight past the scope message to the Export ▾ button — `Select all 31` is never focused.

findings.element: Bulk action bar replacing the table header row (#head-bulk / #head-normal)
findings.finding: Selecting a row sets #head-normal to display:none, which removes every <th> column name from the table, and the swap is announced by nothing — there is no aria-live region and no focus move.
findings.user_impact: A screen-reader user who checks a row loses the column names for every cell they then read ("$340.00" with no "Amount"), and is never told that six destructive bulk actions have appeared where the header used to be.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the header row in the DOM and render the bulk toolbar as a labelled region above the table (role="toolbar" aria-label="Bulk actions") with the selection count in an aria-live="polite" element.

evidence.action: Check one row checkbox, then uncheck it (state map: select-all commit_path; index.html:2704-2724)
evidence.observed: updateBulkBar() hides #head-normal and shows #head-bulk, whose 9 <th> cells are replaced by a single colspan=8 toolbar; the state map records "header row hidden=true" on selection and, after escalating to 31 and unchecking, "uncheck restored header row=false" — so in the exercised path the column headers never came back.

findings.element: Segmented status tabs (All / Needs attention / Ready to sync / In progress / Successful / Deleted)
findings.finding: The tabs are real buttons but expose their selected state only through a CSS class — there is no role="tab"/aria-selected, no aria-pressed and no aria-current anywhere in the file, and the .partial state (segment contains the active status but is narrower than it) has no ARIA equivalent at all.
findings.user_impact: A screen-reader user cannot tell which status tab is active, so on the deep-linked arrival from the Dashboard — where the Status chip says "Failed" and the tab is only partially selected — they have no way to hear which of the two status controls is actually filtering the rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the row in role="tablist" with role="tab" + aria-selected on each segment, and render the partial state as visible text in the accessible name (e.g. "Needs attention, 8, narrowed to Failed").

evidence.action: Inspect the segment builders for variant 1 (renderRecSegments, index.html:3737-3757; renderSegmentsInto, index.html:3634-3653)
evidence.observed: Each button gets only `className = 'status-segment' + (active ? ' active' : '') + (partial ? ' partial' : '')` and `data-segment`; the accessible name is the concatenated text "Needs attention8", identical whether the segment is active, partial or inactive.

gaps: The state map records NO keyboard or focus behaviour for any control on the screen — no tab traversal, no key presses, no focus destinations, no focus-ring observations. Its commit_path fields (picked / reached_apply / still_visible / still_clickable) describe pointer interaction only. Every finding above is therefore derived from the prototype source on disk, not from exercised keyboard behaviour, and the recon needs a keyboard pass before round 2.
No screen-reader pass was run, so every accessible name in this report is computed from markup rather than heard. Announcement order and live-region behaviour are unverified.

Escape is bound at document level to closeAllLayers(), but the state map never records pressing Escape with a panel open — so whether the four filter panels and two menus actually close, and where focus lands afterwards, is unverified.

Focus containment and return for the four dropdown panels (Date range, Platform, Status, Add filter) and the two menus (row ⋯, Export ▾) was never exercised. The file has zero .focus() calls, which strongly implies neither is implemented, but 'focus enters the panel via natural DOM order' vs 'panel is inert' was not tested.

Whether a closed variant-1 dropdown panel is removed from the tab order is unknown. The source documents this care only for the V7 side sheet (visibility:hidden, index.html:352) — which is out of scope this round — and the equivalent was not checked for the variant-1 panels.

Focus visibility could not be confirmed empirically: .panel-search input and .toolbar-search input set outline:none, and .panel-search has no :focus rule at all, but no screenshot of a focused state exists in the recon record, so whether a UA default ring survives on buttons was not observed.

The state map's 'uncheck restored header row=false' was recorded once, after escalating selection to all 31. Whether the header row is also lost on the simpler check-then-uncheck path, or recovers on the next re-render, was not re-tested — A11Y-3's severity rests partly on that single observation.
